posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
618 YishunNoticed the pork lard had some skin and wanted to revisit. This time I noticed the carrot cake stall was open and asked if I can order one. Old aunty said “Yes can and won’t take so long.”. I the ordered a $5.50 HKM + $4 ingredients + egg fried into noodles and + 1 sunny side up. Don’t know why but had two yolks. I think it’s quite common for her eggs to have two yolks.  Carrot cake was just superb. Won’t elaborate but I get why the queue is so long and I won’t mind ordering it and wait while I eat something else.  HKM was mild in flavor but since I added eggs and there were so much ingredients, it was quite a healthy meal. The pork lard and skin….plenty of good fats and collagen. I understand why so many people revisit. It’s relatively healthy compared to some others, and it’s quite a big portion. Prawns were huge and firm, and was nicely seasoned. Glad to have this as the last HKM for this lunar new year. I couldn’t finish and had to waste food. Sigh. I made it up by fasting the rest of the day and made it my only meal for the day. 618 Yishun Ring Rd, Singapore 760618

This stall needs no introduction. If you don’t know this stall, please leave the group. Anyway, jokes aside. Heard of this legendary stall so many times and decided to come try (first time) since I was in the vicinity. Could literally smell the wok hei when I approached the stall. Confirm ho seh liao. Ordered a $7 portion, pretty decent serving size. Waited about 10 mins.First bite. WOK HEIIIII. Solid. Really love the wok hei and mild umami. Noodles were fried really well and still slightly wet and the gooey zhup was just out of this world. Not sure if they offered pork lard, but their pork slices were thick and chunky. 3 medium to large size prawns were fresh. No sotong though. Chilli was not the typical sambal I like but this was quite ok, spicy and sour, goes quite well with the noodles. Overall, superb plate of noodles for me and superb value for $7. PS. I saw their sign board got opeh leave for takeaway, anyone knows if really have? Didn’t had a chance to ask as they were really busy with dinner service.

posts.text:
I must confess, for a HKM aficionado, I have not tried Nam Sing. But definitely not for the lack of trying. Many times I reached Old Airport market only to find them sold out and at other times, the wait was more than 40 min, which prompted me to opt for the other famous brand Yi Ji.This brand has survived since 1960s, and it has a fierce following who defends their style, since it could be their growing up comfort food.So let's be objective. The ingredients were definitely fresh and I found the sotong especially to be very fresh and springy. Chilli to me was disappointing, there is only cut red chilli, and not that of the spicy kind. I hear that's the way the ancients have it, before the advent of belachan and chili padi to the dish.Stock wise not as strong flavored as other well known heavyweights, not so much of prawn umami, instead I can taste they opted for slight seafood umami combined with lots of egg. Overall the dish felt very healthy and not too sinful a delight for a HKM. I can see why this could be a comfort food for many, but it unfortunately doesn't hit strong flavorful notes I would have preferred.@Nam Sing hokkien fried meeOld Airport FC

The Canteen by Enjoy$15.80++ for the HKM. 2 big prawns but not flavorful or juicy. Slightly dry and tasted like those freshwater big head prawns. Claimed to be possibly the best HKM but not on the top 10 on my list. It’s edible and decent, but really not great. It was overly seasoned and had a strong salty taste but also left a “spicy” aftertaste of an excessively seasoned dish. Had two types of bee hoon similar to Fung Yi but of course nothing near that standard. Sotong was rubbery although there were quite a few. Pork was not very flavorful as it felt like the wrong cut of pork was used. Lard was just standard fare. Chilli looked nice but didn’t have much spice nor flavor. Anyway it was a one off and probably pointless to go back for another visit. Other dishes were all pretty average. If you’re thinking of visiting because of the claim of being the best HKM, consider it as me taking one for the team. But if you’re just bored and want to try all the HKM around then maybe you can add this to your list. 383 Jln Besar, Kam Leng Hotel, Singapore 209001

posts.text:
Always wanted to try this stall which is behind my parent’s house. Today finally had the chance. $6 and $9 options available. Accepts paynow. Overall $6 is pretty worth it. Decent sized portion with 3 large prawns. Also got sotong and pork belly, both of which came in pretty chunky pieces. Taste wise it’s tasty, with sufficient umami and prawny taste. It’s the wet and slurpy type, noodles were cooked just about right. The prawns were peeled, and really big and fresh! Auntie asked if I wanted chilli and pork lard, of course want la, still need to ask meh?  Pork lard was decent, most were still crispy. Goes damn well with each spoonful of noodles. As for the chilli, I’m not really a fan of this type of chilli as I prefer the typical sambal. But I did try and it was slightly spicy and sour, but did not overpower the taste of the dish. It’s an above average plate for me. Would definitely come back again when visiting my parent. Lastly, before you start asking “Where?” Please google the stall name la… or look at the tagged location. p.s. the sign board color and pattern look a bit familiar, see liao like very shiok.  anyone knows if any back story?

Shiok HKM Bishan
Didn’t have the intent to post as it was just another day at Shiok Bishan. Other than the wok hei infused creamy gravy that are clinging on to the al dente noodles, I noticed a difference in the pork lard. It now has pieces of pork skin attached and this is a plus because it makes it harder to burn, less oily, more crispy, and overall just more pleasant and goes well with the dish. Congrats to the team for the constant improvements. Keep it up and the skin added to the lard is definitely a positive change.
Again Shiok Bishan’s primary chef is also improving to the point that I think it’s pretty much as good as it gets where skills are involved.
All the best for Sunday’s opening at Woodlands.

Lunch at Bao Er Cafe at Holland V today and was honestly quite disappointed with the HKM.

The moment I slid open the glass door and stepped in, the entire café smelled strongly of smoke. It’s not the pleasant kind of smoky aroma you’d associate with wok hei, but rather the burnt food kind of smell.

I proceeded to order a plate of HKM and added noodles for an additional $2. Unfortunately, the dish tasted exactly like how the café smelled. Some might mistake it for wok hei, but to me, it was clearly burnt. The overall dish had a bitter, charred taste. The eggs were visibly blackened, and the gravy was unusually dark in colour. From the flavour, it seemed like the bitterness came from burnt residue or carbonised bits from the wok and I’m suspecting they do not wash and clean the wok in between batches to retain the burnt residues. 

After eating regularly at other HKM such as Bedok 69 HKM, Hainan HKM, and Youfu, I can confidently say I know the difference between proper wok hei and food that is simply burnt. 

That said, the staff were polite and service was pleasant. The tea and kaya toast were good, and the prawns used in the HKM were sweet and fresh. It’s a pity the execution of the noodles overshadowed what could have been a decent dish.
